verdict.rationale: First-party docs show Ubuntu installs on hardware of the user's choosing. It can replace Windows or dual-boot alongside it from a bootable USB, with install guides covering BitLocker and Intel RST/AHCI. It runs on older machines, is certified on Raspberry Pi (Arm), ships on Dell/HP/Lenovo devices, and has documented NVIDIA driver and DKMS support. Choice of desktop flavours backed by the full archive adds user control. Missing for 10: an explicit vendor-lock-in-free or open-licensing claim (the no-lock-in element is only implied), and independent or hands-on corroboration of broad hardware compatibility.
